thread:
alex: Heads up — getting reports from a customer (corpX) where SSE streams start fine but then stop sending chunks after ~25-40s. Client sees HTTP 200 then silence, reconnects succeed but resume misses partial output.

maria: Can you paste a minimal repro? which route/model, any auth errors?

alex: Using /v1/streams/generate (davinci-like), token auth, POST then stream of events. No 4xx/5xx. Logs show tail: 

```
[2026-03-12T15:03:21Z] conn=abcd auth=ok route=/v1/streams/generate status=200 bytes=512
[2026-03-12T15:03:46Z] conn=abcd keepalive=none last_write=15s closed_by_peer=false
```

alex: Customer is behind an API gateway (corporate gateway + AWS ALB in front of our edge). They said their gateway injects a comment ping every 15s but sometimes strips CRLF.

ingrid: That smells like comment ping vs TCP keepalive mismatch. If gateway rewrites chunks and drops the SSE colon prefix `: ping\n\n` the client may believe stream ended. Do we have logs showing SSE chunks sent after 25s?

alex: Server side shows we sent `: keepalive` at 15s and then another event token output after 30s, but the client didn't receive the event chunk. Client trace attached by customer shows sequence: HTTP 200, data event, comment, silence, then reconnect.

maria: Any proxies that buffer until newline/CRLF? Envoy/NGINX may buffer if `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` chunks malformed. Also ALBs can close idle connections if no bytes in X seconds. But there are bytes (comment pings).

ops-oncall: Quick checks — ask customer to capture tcpdump or `curl -v` to see whether bytes actually flow after the silence. If they can run: 

```
curl -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -N https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate
```

ops-oncall: `-N` disables curl buffering so you can see partial chunks.

alex: They ran curl -N and saw the comment lines sometimes arrive as `\n` only (no colon) on the client side, e.g., `\n` instead of `: keepalive\n\n`. That would make the client parser think there's an empty line (end of event) then nothing.

ingrid: Looks like gateway mangling. Two possibilities: 1) Gateway strips leading `:` (comment char) when it view-modifies headers/body, 2) Gateway converts `\r\n` sequences to `\n` and then later buffers until an extra `\r\n` appears, dropping intermediate chunks.

maria: Could also be TLS terminator reassembling frames and dropping zero-length chunks. Also billing note — the customer reported excess token billing because client retried and resumed with `last-event-id` causing duplicate partial outputs. We should flag potential double-charge flows.

ops-oncall: Repro steps for us to test: 1) Stand up Envoy with streaming timeouts similar to customer's gateway. 2) Use our edge to stream a test model with comment pings every 15s. 3) Vary whether comment pings are sent as `: ping\n\n` vs `\n\n` and see client behavior. 4) Validate Last-Event-ID resume handling and dedupe at application layer.

alex: Customer provided a minimal server snippet they used to send pings: 

```
// pseudo
res.write(": keepalive\r\n\r\n");
res.write("data: {\"chunk\":1}\r\n\r\n");
```

alex: When the gateway rewrites newlines to `\n`, the `: keepalive` becomes `: keepalive\n\n` -> fine; but when it strips the `:` we end up with `keepalive\n\n` which is interpreted as data line `keepalive` (no "data: ") so client sees malformed event and parsers can get stuck.

ingrid: Action items for support team: ask customer for tcpdump (server+client) and `curl -v -N` output, confirm gateway vendor/version and any transform features enabled. Recommend disabling body modification or leaving SSE passthrough.

maria: For product/incidents — we should consider adding an optional `sse_comment_style` that uses `data: \n` empty data heartbeats instead of colon comments for compatibility, or toggleable binary `\x00`-prefixed client-visible heartbeats for gateways that preserve arbitrary bytes. Need engineering input on safety.

ops-oncall: Short-term workaround: advise to set gateway to not reformat chunk boundaries, or enable TCP keepalive on their edge (OS-level) so connections are not considered idle. Also suggest increasing ALB idle timeout > 60s.

alex: Customer also saw stale Last-Event-ID resumes causing duplicate chunks and billing disputes; I created support ticket INC-5409 and flagged billing. Billing team alerted.

maria: I'll coordinate with eng-runtime to run Envoy repro and test alternative heartbeat strategies. tagging @ingrid for kernel-level keepalive docs. :eyes:

support-bot: Incident INC-5409 created, priority P2, assignees: alex, maria, ingrid.

alex: Will follow up with customer tonight with repro steps and temporary config to avoid double-charges. Thanks all :thumbsup:
